item.title: Characterizations for quasiconformal weighted Bergman spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish characterizations of planar quasiconformal mappings in weighted Bergman spaces $A_\alpha^p(\mathbb D)$. For $p>0$ and $\alpha>-1$, our characterization involves the convergence of certain integrals involving superlevel set areas, the Hausdorff measure of boundary superlevel sets, and the averaged derivative. These include quasiconformal analogues of characterizations established by Karafyllia and Karamanlis for conformal mappings. Moreover, for $-1<\alpha\leq 0$, we obtain an additional equivalent characterization in terms of the Hausdorff measure of level sets. The power $\alpha$ is sharp: for every $\alpha>0$, we construct a bounded $K_\alpha$-quasiconformal mapping for which the weighted level-set length integral with exponent $\alpha+2$ diverges.
item.dc:creator: Pekka Koskela, Chengxi Li, Abhishek Pandey

item.title: Absolute moments of GH distribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.14422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we focus on deriving the absolute moments of the general ized hyperbolic (GH) distribution via its mean-variance mixture structure. Conditioning on the GIG mixing variable reduces the problem to Gaussian moment calculations and known GIG power moments, avoiding direct integration with Bessel functions. The variance gamma (VG), normal inverse Gaussian (NIG), hyperbolic, Normal, and Student t distributions emerge as natural special or limiting cases of the generalized hyperbolic family. This approach offers a substantially simpler and more transparent derivation, facilitating both implementation and verification.
item.dc:creator: Chuancun Yin

item.title: Averaged derivatives and reverse inequalities in quasiregular Bergman spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted Bergman spaces of quasiregular mappings on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with weight $(1-|x|)^\alpha$, $\alpha>-1$. For every fixed distortion bound $K\ge1$ and every $p>0$, we characterize Bergman integrability by averaged derivatives. We also give geometric conditions under which integration over a subset, or against another measure, controls the full Bergman integral. When $K$ is sufficiently large, the dominating sets are precisely the relatively dense sets. For comparison, we determine the dominating sets for the M\"obius class $K=1$ in dimensions $n\ge3$. At the critical exponent $p=n+\alpha$, its domination criterion differs from that for every fixed $K>1$. Our results extend aspects of the Bergman theory developed by Nolder~\cite{Nolder90} and by Oleinik and Vuorinen~\cite{OV}, and complement the recent work of Adamowicz and Gonz\'alez~\cite{AG21,AG25} and Adamowicz and Caama\~no~\cite{AC} on quasiregular Hardy spaces.
item.dc:creator: Suman Das

item.title: Uniform Green packing on compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on Laplace designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with the help of ChatGPT.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.15004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Maximum-modulus points on concentric circles
item.description:
arXiv:2610.15067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a nonzero, non-monomial entire function, and let $
u_f(r)$ count the points at which $f$ attains its maximum modulus on $|z|=r$. Write $f(z)=z^m(a_0+a_kz^k+O(z^{k+1}))$, where $a_0a_k
e0$. We prove that $
u_f(r)\le 2k$ outside a locally finite subset of $(0,\infty)$. The constant $2k$ is sharp. In particular, $\liminf_{r	o\infty}
u_f(r)<\infty$, so the number of maximum-modulus points of a fixed non-monomial entire function cannot tend to infinity on all sufficiently large circles. The proof associates the logarithmic derivative $q=zf'/f$ with its reflection $q^*(w)=\overline{q( ar w)}$ through the correspondence $q(z)=q^*(w)$ and the map $(z,w)\mapsto(zw,q(z))$. Local valence at the origin bounds the number of inverse pairs that can escape. A local elimination argument then bounds the generic degree of each nonvertical image component. The residue structure of $f'/f$ excludes vertical components.
item.dc:creator: Yunpeng Li

item.title: A computer-assisted proof of Krzy\.z's conjecture for the sixth coefficient
item.description: arXiv:2610.15206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Krzy\.z's conjecture for the sixth coefficient. Every holomorphic function $f(z)=\sum a_kz^k$ from the unit disk to the punctured disk satisfies $|a_6| \le 2/e$. Equality holds precisely for rotations of $\exp(-(1-z^6)/(1+z^6))$. Every extremal has a Herglotz representation with at most six atoms. By the reduction of Agler and McCarthy and the entropy theorem of Lei and Zhang, it suffices to exclude extremals with fewer than six atoms. We do this by a rigorous computer-assisted branch-and-bound, leaving the equality case entirely to the analytic argument. The main ingredients are explicit first-order conditions for extremals with fewer than the maximal number of atoms, which reduce to Chebyshev relations when one atom is missing, and a bound for the total mass obtained by convexity of the Poisson integral. The same method independently establishes the full-degree property for the known cases $n=3,4,5$.
item.dc:creator: Frank Wikstr\"om

item.title: Quaternionic Elasticity Theory with Local Fractional Derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2610.15304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a quaternionic formulation of linear elasticity in which the classical derivative is replaced by Yang's local fractional derivative and the classical Cauchy--Riemann operator by a fractal Cauchy--Riemann operator. We formulate fractal kinematics, a constitutive law with a material length scale and the equilibrium equation, and show that, for displacement fields with polynomial components, the resulting homogeneous fractal Lam\'e system is equivalent to the monogenicity of an explicit quaternionic field. On the polynomial sector, that is, for finite combinations of normalized fractal monomials, we prove a fractal Kolosov--Muskhelishvili representation of the displacement field in terms of two monogenic quaternionic potentials, together with its completeness, by a direct construction that uses neither the Galerkin nor the Papkovich--Neuber potentials. The position term of the classical formula has to be replaced by a corrected position operator, which satisfies the exact Weyl relation with the partial local fractional derivatives. Finally a fractal Papkovich-Neuber representation is derived.
item.dc:creator: Hung Manh Nguyen, Juan Bory-Reyes

item.title: The sharp constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.15378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the optimal constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality is $e$, as conjectured by Andreev and Matheson. More precisely, if $f$ is analytic in the unit disk, vanishes to order $m\geq1$ at the origin, and has normalized Dirichlet integral $d\leq1$, then the boundary mean of $e^{|f|^2}$ is at most $e^{d/m}$. Equality holds precisely for monomials. The proof uses an auxiliary closed planar curve and the isoperimetric inequality to establish monotonicity of the exponential functional along normalized radial dilations.
item.dc:creator: Rupert L. Frank, Paata Ivanisvili

item.title: Oka complements in algebraic tori and their logarithmic covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.15433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $K\subset\C^n$ is compact and polynomially convex. Write $q(z)=(e^{-iz_1},\ldots,e^{-iz_n})$, $X_K=(\C^*)^n\setminus(K\cap(\C^*)^n)$, and $Y_K=\C^n\setminus q^{-1}(K)$. We prove that $X_K$ and its logarithmic covering $Y_K$ are Oka. More strongly, $Y_K$ admits normalized holomorphic families of entire embeddings through prescribed holomorphic sections. The proof combines polynomial pair Hamiltonian transport in multiplicative coordinates, compatible with the coordinate hyperplanes, with a fixed Fatou--Bieberbach model. Applications include Oka slab crosses over arbitrary nonempty connected planar domains, complements of periodic equal-radius Euclidean balls centered at products of planar lattices, and complements of sufficiently small closed metric balls in products of elliptic curves.
item.dc:creator: Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Toeplitz determinants for starlike mappings of order {\alpha} in several complex variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.15497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F(z)=zf(z)$, where $f$ is a normalized scalar holomorphic function on the unit ball $\mathbb B$ of a complex Banach space $X$ or on the unit polydisk $\mathbb U^n$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$. We establish sharp bounds for two Toeplitz determinants involving the second, third and fourth Fr\'echet derivatives of $F$ when $F$ is starlike of order $\alpha$, $0\leq\alpha<1$. The first bound is sharp for the full range $0\leq\alpha<1$, while the second is sharp for $0\leq\alpha\leq 2/3$. The extremal mappings are explicitly identified, confirming the sharpness of the estimates.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Panja, Sujoy Majumder, Abhijit Banerjee

item.title: On Mok's uniqueness problem of holomorphic isometries from complex unit balls of maximal dimension into classical domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.15637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every holomorphic isometric embedding, with respect to the Bergman metrics, from a complex unit ball of maximal dimension into irreducible classical bounded symmetric domain of rank at least two that is not biholomorphic to a Type IV domain is equivalent to Mok's embedding. This completely resolves a problem of Mok.
item.dc:creator: Cong Ding, Yuan Yuan

item.title: The Fekete-Szeg\"{o} problem for starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ and quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit balls of complex Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp estimates for the generalized Zalcman functional corresponding to the index $n=2$ for normalized starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ and normalized quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit ball of a complex Banach space and on the unit polydisk in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We also derive sharp Fekete-Szeg\"{o} inequalities for normalized starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ and normalized quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit ball of a complex Banach space. Our results extend classical coefficient estimates to higher-dimensional holomorphic mappings and provide a partial confirmation of the generalized Zalcman conjecture in higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Majumder, Abhijit Banerjee, Goutam Haldar, Shantanu Panja

item.title: The Bloch constant is strictly smaller than the Ahlfors--Grunsky value
item.description: arXiv:2610.16808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the classical Bloch constant is strictly smaller than the Ahlfors--Grunsky value, disproving the famous Bloch constant conjecture. The Lean 4 formalization of the main results are also provided.
item.dc:creator: Teng Zhang

item.title: Oka realizations, fundamental groups, and holomorphic cofibrations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The homotopy types of Oka manifolds are exactly those of countable finite-dimensional CW complexes. We construct realizations as open subsets of complex Euclidean spaces with explicit dimension bounds. Other realizations have good open covers by sets biholomorphic to $\C^N$, with prescribed finite nerves, or are unions of Fatou--Bieberbach domains whose nonempty finite intersections are again Fatou--Bieberbach domains. Every nonempty Stein manifold admits a proper holomorphic embedding into an Oka open subset of some $\C^N$, and this embedding is a homotopy equivalence. We obtain holomorphic representatives of ordinary and generalized cohomology classes, and realize every countable group as the fundamental group of an Oka domain in $\C^5$. The fundamental groups of algebraically elliptic manifolds are precisely the finite groups, and every virtually abelian K\"ahler group is the fundamental group of a projective Oka manifold. Finally, we classify holomorphic cofibrations in L\'arusson's intermediate model structures and establish factorizations over aspherical targets into proper holomorphic embeddings and holomorphic fibre bundles with Oka fibre.
item.dc:creator: Bin Guo, Yuta Kusakabe, Peng-Chao Wang

item.title: Fermat's Last Theorem in star-invariant subspaces II: small boundary spectrum, projective plane curves, and the cubic Fermat equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.17180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study algebraic relations among functions in star-invariant subspaces. Let $\theta$ be an inner function and suppose that $f,g,h\in K_{\theta}^p$ satisfy $P(f,g,h)=0$, in which $P$ is a homogeneous polynomial and the associated projective plane curve is smooth. Then $\dim\operatorname{span}\{f,g,h\}\leq1$ if either $\operatorname{deg} P\geq 4$ and the boundary spectrum of $\theta$ has logarithmic capacity zero, or $\operatorname{deg} P = 3$ and the boundary spectrum contains at most one point. This settles new cases of a problem of Dyakonov, subsumes the previously known results, and recovers the classical fact that polynomial parametrizations of a smooth projective plane curve of degree at least three are projectively constant.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Ramon Garcia

item.title: On the rank-one limit sets for maps in the constant-Jacobian shear group of $\mathbb{C}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_c$ be the subgroup of $Aut(\mathbb{C}^2)$ generated by affine maps and shear automorphisms with constant Jacobian. We determine the possible conformal types of the rank-one limit set of an invariant recurrent Fatou component when the induced dynamics has infinite order. In particular we show that, under this infinite-order hypothesis, the limit set of a finite composition of H\'enon maps (polynomial or transcendental), can only be conformally equivalent to a disk or an annulus. Thus we exclude the remaining three conformal types, i.e. $\mathbb{D}^*$, $\mathbb{C}^*$ and $\mathbb{C}$, from the classification result by Arosio, Benini, Forn\ae ss and Peters. We also prove that the set of fixed points of a finite composition of H\'enon maps (polynomial or transcendental) contains no entire curves.
item.dc:creator: Luka Boc Thaler

item.title: On horn-shaped Reinhardt domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.17527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of unbounded Reinhardt domains in $\mathbb C^n$ ($n\geq 2$),which we call horn domains. We study the dimensions of the Bergman spaces,the holomorphic sectional curvature of the Bergman metric, and the holomorphic equivalence problem for such horn Reinhardt domains.
item.dc:creator: Chika Hayashida, Joe Kamimoto, Ninh Van Thu

item.title: Large deviation principle for determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.17669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study natural determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds defined by canonical sections and plurisubharmonic weight functions. We present a natural condition on the weights under which these processes satisfy a large deviation principle with a good rate function given by the Fenchel--Legendre transform of the pluripotential equilibrium energy. Along the way, we prove some pluripotential theoretic results on Stein manifolds, such as the $C^{1,1}$ regularity of appropriate envelopes. These results are noncompact analogues of results of Berman and Berman--Boucksom on compact K\"ahler manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Kiyoon Eum

item.title: A converse to Littlewood-type theorem for random Dirichlet series
item.description: arXiv:2610.17876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article investigates random Dirichlet series within the framework of Hardy and mixed norm spaces of Dirichlet series. We completely characterize when the random symbol space of the Hardy space $\mathscr{H}^p$ coincides with $\mathscr{H}^2$. In the setting of mixed norm spaces $\mathscr{H}^{p,q}_{\alpha}$, the corresponding characterizations for the random symbol space of $\mathscr{H}^{p,q}_{\alpha}$ coinciding with $\mathscr{H}^{2,q}_{\alpha}$ are given when $q\geq4$, and some sufficient and necessary conditions are established when $q<4$. We also obtain some integrability results when Dirichlet series belong to the corresponding random symbol spaces.
item.dc:creator: Jiale Chen, Min He, Maofa Wang

item.title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14266v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $\tau\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_\tau g(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \tau_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $\tau\mapsto T_\tau$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_\tau$ to the inverse of $\tau$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $\tau$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $\tau$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Julian Billner, Cornelia Schneider

item.title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.14291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $\deg p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=\alpha\,q(\beta z+h)+k$ or $p(z)=\alpha\,\bar q(\beta z+h)+k$ for some $\alpha,\beta,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Fernandes, Claudia Fernandes, Edson Sampaio

item.title: A counterexample concerning the coefficient formula for de Branges-Rovnyak norms
item.description: arXiv:2610.15019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}(b)$ be the de Branges-Rovnyak space associated to a non-extreme point $b$ of the unit ball of $H^\infty$, and let $\phi=b/a$, where $a$ is the Pythagorean mate of $b$. In an earlier article, the author showed that, if $\phi\in H^2$, then \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b) \iff \Bigl(f\in H^2 \text{ and }\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr), \] in which case we have \[ \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}(b)}^2=\sum_{m\ge0}|\hat{f}(m)|^2 +\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2. \] It was also shown that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $\phi\in\cap_{p<2}H^p$, yet \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b)\not\Rightarrow \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty. \] Here we complete this circle of ideas by showing that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $\phi\in\cap_{p<1}H^p$, yet \[ \Bigl(f\in H^2\text{ and } \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr) \not\Rightarrow f\in\mathcal{H}(b). \]
item.dc:creator: Thomas Ransford

item.title: Plane wave representation for wave scattering on a sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.15121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.
item.dc:creator: Valentin D. Kunz, Andrey V. Shanin, Raphael C. Assier

item.title: Sparsity and uniformity in dynamical Manin--Mumford problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.15169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For endomorphisms of the complex projective plane of a given degree, we prove that the existence of a special curve of bounded degree, in the sense of the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture, is confined to a proper algebraic subvariety of the parameter space. This confirms a conjecture of DeMarco and Mavraki in dimension two. For general regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb A^k$, we obtain a uniform dynamical Manin--Mumford bound outside an exceptional hypersurface. These results arise from a common strategy, valid in every dimension and codimension, which reduces such questions to the geometry of exceptional loci in the space of pairs formed by subvarieties and maps. We control these loci by combining arithmetic equidistribution, blender constructions, dynamical directions, monodromy arguments, and degenerations at the boundary of parameter space.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Gauthier, Johan Taflin

item.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.15736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.
item.dc:creator: Allen Weitsman

item.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of K\"ahler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform \`a priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.
item.dc:creator: Johannes G. Scheffler

item.title: Contractivity of Rudin's diagonal restriction operator for $H^p$ of the polydisc
item.description: arXiv:2610.16227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish that Rudin's diagonal restriction operator is contractive from the Hardy space $H^p$ of the bidisc to the Bergman space $A^p$ of the disc for $2\leq p<\infty$, and characterize all cases of equality. We extend the result to polydiscs and obtain applications to polynomial point evaluation among others. The proof relies on an explicit formula, deduced from certain Green's formulas, for the defect between the $p$th powers of the two $L^p$ norms.
item.dc:creator: Ole Fredrik Brevig, Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Joaquim Ortega-Cerd\`{a}, Kristian Seip

item.title: Fatou Components of Attracting Skew Products: From Polynomial Classification to Transcendental Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2610.16583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Fatou components of holomorphic skew products $F \colon \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2, F(z,w) = (f(z) + r(z,w), g(w))$ near an attracting invariant fiber, introducing a refined classification of components on the fiber: bulging, partial bulging, and nowhere bulging. For polynomial skew products, we give a complete characterization of when the basin at infinity is non-bulging, and show that in this case non-bulging implies nowhere bulging, ruling out partial bulging entirely. In the transcendental setting, the behavior is richer: we construct partially bulging wandering domains and Baker domains, show that any orbitally unbounded Fatou component can be made nowhere bulging by choosing an appropriate function $r$, and prove that for any nonconstant $r$ there exists an entire function $f$ with an escaping wandering domain that fails to be bulging. Bulging thus depends on the interplay between fiber dynamics and perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Tom Potthink

item.title: Interpolation by Rational $\Gamma_{E(3; 3; 1, 1, 1)}$-Inner Function and Rational $\Gamma_{E(3; 2; 1, 2)}$-Inner Function
item.description: arXiv:2610.16779v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study several function-theoretic aspects of the domains $G_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$ and $G_{E(3;2;1,2)}$. We introduce and investigate the notions of $\Gamma_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$-inner functions and $\Gamma_{E(3;2;1,2)}$-inner functions, and establish their relationships with $\Gamma_{E(2;2;1,1)}$-inner functions and $\Gamma_{E(2;1;2)}$-inner functions. We provide explicit constructions and representations of rational $\Gamma_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$-inner functions and rational $\Gamma_{E(3;2;1,2)}$-inner functions. As an application of these results, we obtain partial solutions to the associated interpolation problems and construct explicit rational inner interpolants for interpolation data lying in suitable subsets of $G_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$ and $G_{E(3;2;1,2)}$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Avijit Pal, Bhaskar Paul

item.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.
item.dc:creator: Sheng Tan

item.title: Purely non-free actions on Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A group of conformal automorphisms of a Riemann surface is said to act purely non-free, or to produce a gpnf-action, if each of its finite-order elements has fixed points. It is known that every finite group admits a gpnf-action on a suitable closed Riemann surface of genus at least two. If $G$ is an infinite countable group, and $X$ is an infinite-type orientable surface, without planar ends and whose space of ends is self-similar, then we observe that there is a Riemann surface structure on $X$ admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. We obtain upper bounds for those finite groups producing a gpnf-action on a closed Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. If $G$ is a finite group, then its purely non-free genus $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$ is the minimum genus of at least two of a closed Riemann surface admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. This parameter is already known for cyclic, abelian non-cyclic groups, ${\mathcal A}_{4}$, ${\mathcal A}_{5}$ and ${\mathfrak S}_{4}$. For general $G$, we provide the value of $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$, correcting a previous statement on this value. In particular, we observe that every genus is the purely non-free genus of some group. As an application, we describe the minimal purely non-free actions for the family of metacyclic groups $G^{0}_{s}(n)=\langle x,y: x^{n}=y^{2}=1, yxy=x^{s}\rangle,$ where $n \geq 3$ and $2 \leq s \leq n-1$ is such that $s^{2} \equiv 1 \mod(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Rub\'en A. Hidalgo, Jhony S. Leyca

item.title: Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Pentablock
item.description: arXiv:2610.17729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The pentablock is a domain in $\mathbb C^3$ arising in the study of the $\mu$-synthesis problem and is defined by \[ \mathcal P = \left\{ (a_{21},\operatorname{tr}(A),\det(A)): A=[a_{ij}]_{i,j=1}^2\in M_2(\mathbb C),\ \|A\|<1 \right\}. \] We introduce the Hardy space $H^2(\mathcal P)$ associated with the canonical measure $\mu$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathcal P$. We identify $H^2(\mathcal P)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathcal P,\mu)$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We establish a new description of $\mathcal P$ and its closure and obtain a uniqueness set. In particular, we prove that $\mathcal P$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $\Psi(\overline{\mathbb D}^3)$, where \[ \Psi(\xi,\lambda_1,\lambda_2) = \left( \frac{\xi(\lambda_1-\lambda_2)}{2}, \lambda_1+\lambda_2, \lambda_1\lambda_2 \right) \] is the parametrization map for $\mathcal P$. We also show that $H^2(\mathcal P)$ embeds isometrically as a closed subspace of $H^2(\mathbb D^3)$. We then obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathcal P)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathcal P$-isometries and their minimal $\mathcal P$-unitary extensions. As consequences, we determine the commutant of the coordinate multipliers, characterize the compact Toeplitz operators and show that the coordinate multipliers have no nontrivial joint reducing subspaces. Finally, we characterize $\mathcal P$-unitaries as images of commuting triples of unitaries under $\Psi$ and present a class of $\mathcal P$-contractions from triples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set.
item.dc:creator: Guicong Su, Nitin Tomar

item.title: The Brownian bubble tea
item.description: arXiv:2610.17990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use Loewner-Kufarev evolution to decompose the Brownian loop soup into a Poisson point process on Brownian bubbles which we call the Brownian bubble tea driven by $\rho$, where $\rho$ is the driving measure for the Loewner chain. The only assumption on $\rho$ is that the evolving boundaries are locally connected. This generalizes a similar disintegration result of Lawler and Werner to essentially optimal regularity, and includes foliations with finite Loewner-Kufarev energy as well as radial and whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ for all $\kappa \geqslant 0$. As applications, we give Brownian loop interpretations of the conformal distortion formula for Loewner-Kufarev energy and the relationships between the Loewner energy, Loewner-Kufarev energy, and the Schwarzian action.
item.dc:creator: Gregory F. Lawler, Fredrik Viklund, Yilin Wang, Catherine Wolfram

item.title: A universal $\overline\partial$ solution operator on nonsmooth strongly pseudoconvex domains
item.description: arXiv:2412.20312v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a universal family of $\overline\partial$ homotopy operators on bounded $C^{1,1}$ domains that are locally strongly $\mathbb C$-linearly convexifiable. In particular this includes $C^2$ strongly pseudoconvex domains and $C^{1,1}$ strongly $\mathbb C$-linearly convex domains. The operators satisfy Sobolev estimates $\mathcal H_q:H^{s,p}\to H^{s+1/2,p}$ and H\"older-Zygmund estimates $\mathcal H_q:\mathscr C^s\to\mathscr C^{s+1/2}$ simultaneously for all $s\in\mathbb R$ and $1<p<\infty$. The construction uses a modification of the Leray-Koppelman formula and a refined directional decomposition of the commutator $[\overline\partial,\mathcal E]$.
item.dc:creator: Liding Yao

item.title: Jets of flat partial connections
item.description: arXiv:2505.11662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define and study jets of flat partial connections in the setting of smooth foliations and flat partial connections on locally free sheaves. In the case of codimension one foliations, we apply this definition to characterize transversely affine and transversely projective structures. For foliations of arbitrary codimension, we use jets of the Bott connection on the normal sheaf to define the prolongation of a transversely projective structure, and then apply it to produce singular transversely projective structures.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Fazoli

item.title: On the k-th Milnor and k-th Tjurina Numbers of a Foliation
item.description: arXiv:2510.24868v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notions of the $k$-th Milnor number and the $k$-th Tjurina number for a germ of holomorphic foliation on the complex plane with an isolated singularity at the origin. We develop a detailed study of these invariants, establishing explicit formulas and relating them to other indices associated with holomorphic foliations. In particular, we obtain an explicit expression for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation and, as a consequence, a formula for the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function. We analyze their topological behavior, proving that the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant, whereas the $k$-th Tjurina number is not. In dimension two, we provide a positive answer to a conjecture posed by Hussain, Liu, Yau, and Zuo concerning a sharp lower bound for the $k$-th Tjurina number of a weighted homogeneous polynomial. We also present a counterexample to another conjecture of Hussain, Yau, and Zuo regarding the ratio between these invariants. Moreover, we establish a fundamental relation linking the $k$-th Tjurina numbers of a foliation and of an invariant curve via the G\'omez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index, and we extend Teissier's Lemma to the setting of $k$-th polar intersection numbers. In addition, we derive an upper bound for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation in terms of its $k$-th Tjurina number along balanced divisors of separatrices. Finally, for non-dicritical quasi-homogeneous foliations, we obtain a closed formula for their $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers.
item.dc:creator: Marcela Ribeiro, Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez

item.title: A Generalization of Zalcman's Lemma on Complex Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.20536v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Zalcman's lemma makes significant applications in normal families, complex dynamics and many other related problems in complex analysis. It is interesting to explore a global version of Zalcman's lemma for complex manifolds, even though normality is a local property. In this paper, we establish a version of Zalcman's lemma for complex Lie groups via exponential mappings.
item.dc:creator: Xianjing Dong, Yanda Lv, Lanjuan Xu

item.title: Remarks on a result of Sibony on the Carath\'eodory topology
item.description: arXiv:2512.03901v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that if a Carath\'eodory hyperbolic analytic space $X$ is $C_X$-complete, then its natural topology is induced by the Carath\'eodory distance on $X$. This is an improvement of Sibony's result, which concludes the same under the hypothesis that $X$ is $C_X$-finitely compact. This improvement is not merely formal; we also show the existence of uncountably many biholomorphically inequivalent analytic spaces that are not $C_X$-finitely compact but are $C_X$-complete.
item.dc:creator: Sudip Dolai

item.title: Sharp degree bound for rational proper maps from $\mathbb B^2$ to $\mathbb B^4$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every rational proper holomorphic map from $\mathbb{B}^2$ to $\mathbb{B}^4$ has degree at most $5$, confirming D'Angelo's conjecture in this case. This sharp bound follows from Meylan's degree estimates and an intersection-theoretic argument ruling out degree $6$.
item.dc:creator: Tianzhi Hu, Mai Shi, Pingsan Yuan

item.title: A Local Approximation Characterization of Oka Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10475v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize Oka manifolds by the local approximation property (LAP), a planar approximation operation that preserves holomorphic dependence on prescribed parameter polydiscs. We prove that LAP yields convex approximation in every source dimension and propagates across sets of zero $(2n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure in an $n$-dimensional target. Consequently, strong dominability characterizes Oka manifolds, convex approximation in the target dimension suffices, the Oka property is local in the Euclidean topology, and it descends under surjective holomorphic maps. Local families of entire curves give geometric applications: smooth projective rationally connected manifolds are Oka, and deleting an algebraic subset of codimension at least two from any such manifold preserves the Oka property. Structure theorems further show that compact K\"ahler manifolds with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature or nef tangent bundle are Oka. Finally, the complement of a smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^n$ is Oka exactly when $d\leq n+1$.
item.dc:creator: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Oka manifolds are ubiquitous
item.description: arXiv:2610.10493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a holomorphic family of connected complex Lie groups is Oka if and only if its base is Oka. We establish the Oka property for moduli spaces of stable and parabolic vector bundles and characterize Oka minimal \(\delta\)-regular abelian fibrations over compact curves by the nonnegativity of their orbifold Euler characteristic. Strong dominability, analytic extension, and holomorphic descent also yield applications to mapping spaces, character varieties, and compactified Jacobians.
item.dc:creator: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Computing the Topological Degree of Maps Between 2-Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2509.20167v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe an effective method for computing the topological degree of continuous functions $R:S^2 \to S^2$, where $S^2$ is the Riemann sphere. Our approach generalizes the degree formula for rational functions of complex polynomials, $\frac{f}{g}$, without common zeros. To apply our method, it is necessary to represent the function $R$ as the ratio of two continuous complex-valued functions $f$ and $g$ without common zeros. By using the Hopf fibration, this method reduces the problem to computing the winding number of a loop. This enables us to compute the degree of $\frac{f}{g}$ even when $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary continuous complex functions without common zeros, and the fraction has a limit at infinity (which can be finite or infinite). Specifically, if $f$ and $g$ are complex polynomials in $z$ and $\bar{z}$, and the highest-degree homogeneous component of the polynomial with the greater algebraic degree has a finite or infinite limit as $|z|\to\infty$, then the problem reduces to counting the roots of a complex polynomial inside the unit circle, obtained from this component.
item.dc:creator: Daniil Kucher

item.title: Bounded Toeplitz operators and unbounded projected multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2601.10711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a smooth, nonnegative radial symbol $g$ on $\mathbb C$ whose Toeplitz operator on Bargmann--Fock space is positive with singular values decaying faster than every exponential, while projected multiplication $f\mapsto P(gf)$ has no bounded extension from the ambient Gaussian $L^2$ space. All heat transforms of $g$ at positive times are Schwartz functions, and $g\in L^p(dA)$ for every $0<p<2$. We also construct smooth real symbols realizing every possible set of heat boundedness times. Any prescribed positive threshold may be included or excluded, with Schwartz transforms at every later time. All these symbols satisfy the coherent state domain condition, and all heat integrals converge absolutely.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: Wave scattering by a transversal defect in a discrete waveguide
item.description: arXiv:2602.10227v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study wave scattering by a finite transversal strip in a discrete square-lattice waveguide with Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on the strip and the waveguide walls. The setting is motivated as a discrete analogue of the classical continuous waveguide problem with a screen. The corresponding Wiener--Hopf formulation leads to an equation with a $4 \times 4$ matrix kernel, which reduces to a $2 \times 2$ matrix kernel under some symmetry assumptions. The prospects for factorising this kernel are discussed, but this approach is not pursued. Instead, an exact analytical solution is obtained using the pole removal technique. This contrasts with the continuous case, where only approximate solutions are currently available. The reflection and transmission coefficients resulting from an incident duct mode are computed with an accuracy up to $10^{-13}$, showing consistency with theoretical predictions from continuous waveguide theory. In particular, full reflection and zero transmission are recovered as the frequency approaches the cut-off value for the incident mode. Finally, the solution is validated against a numerical computation of the diffraction problem via the Boundary Algebraic Equations method with a tailored lattice Green's function.
item.dc:creator: Elena Medvedeva, Raphael Assier, Anastasia Kisil

item.title: Heat Kernel and Resurgence
item.description: arXiv:2606.21909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the resurgent structure of short--time heat kernel asymptotics from the viewpoint of Picard--Lefschetz theory. For a real analytic Riemannian manifold, we show the heat kernel admits a 1-- Gevrey small--time expansion whose Borel transform detects complex--geometric data beyond the real geodesic sector. We formulate an infinite--dimensional Picard--Lefschetz problem of Morse--Floer type for the holomorphic energy functional on the complexified path space, and propose a heat--kernel analogue of the Picard--Lefschetz/Alien correspondence. In this framework, pointed alien operators acting on the asymptotic expansion associated with the real geodesic are predicted to produce the formal heat--kernel sectors associated with other holomorphic geodesics, with coefficients given by signed counts of connecting trajectories of the Morse flow. We perform a confirming test of this proposal on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}_{\R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Si Li, Yong Li, Xinxing Tang

item.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2609.25762v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the relation between canonical positivity, rigidity of a prescribed Hermitian metric, and the curvature not detected by Chern holomorphic sectional curvature. A compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold admitting an independent smooth plurinegative Hermitian metric is projective with ample canonical bundle. In Fujiki's class, nonpositive constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature forces the original metric to be K\"ahler. On compact complex threefolds, without an auxiliary metric or a Fujiki-class assumption, a nonzero constant forces K\"ahlerness. We also give an alternative proof of Chen--Zheng's Chern-flatness theorem for zero-HSC threefolds, by proving local rank-two differential compatibility and localizing their curvature bound under $\partial\eta=0$. In contrast, for every complex dimension at least seven we give compact balanced zero-HSC metrics with nonzero Chern curvature. Their octonionic curvature formula also implies the vanishing of all four Chern--Ricci contractions, and an explicit invariant volume form is Chern parallel. Finally, an auxiliary semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form, positive definite at some point, restores flat K\"ahlerness under zero HSC and vanishing first Chern--Ricci tensor. A mixed Ricci integral criterion explains the role of this last curvature hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin, Yuanhong Tian

item.title: Codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2609.37695v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected complex manifold is biholomorphically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of a complex torus. This verifies a conjecture of Ghys in the codimension-one case and, in particular, in complex dimension three.
item.dc:creator: Jiesong Zhang

item.title: Dolbeault Cohomology Growth under Curvature Rank Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.09295v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $L$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, and let $r$ be its maximal curvature rank. For every fixed holomorphic vector bundle $E$, we prove $h^q(X,L^p\otimes E)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every Dolbeault degree, with the sharp bounds $h^0,h^n=O(p^r)$ at the endpoints. The curvature may have variable rank and arbitrary signature, and no global foliation or K\"ahler assumption is imposed. The all-degree estimate follows from local rescaling and holomorphic restriction estimates that remain uniform across rank changes. An independent maximum-principle argument locates the maximal rank of a section map at a semipositive curvature point; it yields $\kappa(L|_{X_0})\le r$ on each connected component $X_0$ and gives the endpoint bounds.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin

item.title: Rational curves on toroidal compactifications of Picard modular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.12071v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It was known that the canonical bundle of a smooth toroidal compactification of a noncompact finite-volume ball quotient is nef in dimension $n\geq3$ and ample in dimension $n\geq6$. We prove that the canonical bundle is ample in dimension $n\geq4$ and show that this dimension bound is sharp. We construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular threefolds whose smooth projective toroidal compactifications have non-ample canonical bundle. Each compactification contains a smooth rational curve meeting the interior and having canonical degree zero. More generally, in every dimension $n\geq2$, we construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular varieties whose smooth toroidal compactifications contain smooth rational curves meeting the interior. In particular, such curves persist in arbitrarily high dimension, even when the canonical bundle is ample.
item.dc:creator: Soheil Memariansorkhabi, Sai-Kee Yeung
